RE: ADU U DC Amendment
Cheyenne, Wyoming
Dec 19, 2025
To Whom It May Concern:
This letter is being submitted to support changes to local requirements governing owner occupancy
on properties with Accessory Dwelling Units(ADUs).Habitat believes this reform advances our
community's goals around housing afford ability and supply
Cheyenne and Wyoming face a significant housing shortage.According to theWCDA's2024
Housing Needs Assessment,20,700-38,600 units areneeded statewide to meet current and future
demand, andbetween4,386and7,266needed for Laramie County.This shortage drives up prices
squeezes families out of home ownership, and increases rent burdens for workers.Without action,
these pressures will continue to displace residents and strain our local economy.
restore afford ability, and also aligns with the WCD A's Statewide Housing Strategic Plan, specifically
These homes provide naturally affordable options for families, seniors, andworkers, whilemaking
better useof existing infrastructure.
Our hope is that these changes will:
·Encourage development and permitting of AD Us.
Expand housing choices for residents at all income levels.
Promote sustainable development by using land more efficiently.
We urge decision-makers to adopt these reforms promptly.By legalizing non-owner occupied ADUs,
Cheyenne can take another step toward closing its housing gap and preserving the character and
livability of our community.
Thank you foryour consideration.
Sincerely,
Dan Dorsch, Executive Director, Habitat for Humanity of Laramie County
